approved: Superannuation Legislation Amendment (Fair Super for Young Workers) Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
as explained in the linked explanatory memorandum
This bill would remove the age-based exemption that currently keeps many employees under eighteen outside compulsory employer superannuation.
Young employees would no longer have to work more than thirty hours in a week to overcome that exemption.
The changes would commence on the day after Royal Assent.
Removes the power to exclude under-eighteen employees, their work or their earnings through the relevant regulations.
Repeals the regulation exempting under-eighteen employees who work thirty hours or less a week.
Applies the change from the day after assent rather than introducing a staged commencement.
Employees under eighteen and employers responsible for their superannuation contributions are affected.

Introduced the Superannuation Legislation Amendment (Fair Super for Young Workers) Bill 2026, arguing the current rule exempting workers under 18 who work fewer than 30 hours a week from compulsory superannuation denies about 530,000 teenage workers a combined $411 million a year, with the debate also raising concerns about how the change would interact with the newly commenced payday super system.

Moved that senators be discharged from and appointed to various committees, including the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, the Economics Legislation and References Committees, and the new Select Committee on Women's Health chaired with members Marielle Smith, Stewart, Waters and Whiteaker.
